noise-ceiling.definition: the best held-out score any model could reach on a target, given how far repeated measurements of that same target disagree; it is estimated from the data's own repeats
noise-ceiling.excludes: the best score reached so far by any model, and a bound set by missing variables

held-out-skill.definition: a model's score on cases kept apart from fitting: R2 for numbers, the area under the ROC curve for yes-or-no outcomes, and accuracy for triplet choices
held-out-skill.excludes: the score on the data used to fit the model

auc.definition: the area under the ROC curve: the chance that a randomly chosen positive case is ranked above a randomly chosen negative one, with 0.5 for guessing

ridge.definition: least squares with a penalty on the size of the coefficients, chosen by leave-one-out error, so that many variables can be fitted without chasing noise
ridge.excludes: non-linear models such as boosted trees or neural networks

share-of-ceiling.definition: held-out skill above chance divided by the noise ceiling above chance; 1 means the model scores as well as the measurements allow
share-of-ceiling.excludes: the raw skill, which is not comparable across targets

saturating-fit.definition: the curve s(k) = a k / (k + h) fitted to skill above chance against the number of variables k, where a is the level it approaches
saturating-fit.excludes: a forecast of skill with variables not in the dataset

brier.definition: the mean squared difference between a probability forecast and the outcome coded 0 or 1; lower is better
brier.excludes: measures that score only whether the most likely outcome happened

split-half.definition: the correlation between scores computed on two halves of the same items, here a forecaster's accuracy on the odd and the even questions
split-half.excludes: agreement between different people or different occasions

parallel-forms.definition: two items meant to measure the same thing, answered at the same time; their correlation estimates reliability, here happy and cheerful at the same beep
parallel-forms.excludes: the same item repeated later, which also picks up real change

strong-variable.definition: a variable of a different kind from the base set, named for each target before the run: past behaviour of the same unit, or a human rating of a related quantity
strong-variable.excludes: one more variable of the kind already in the base set

lorenz-horizon.definition: the time until a forecast from a slightly wrong starting state differs from the truth by more than a set tolerance; in a chaotic system it grows with the logarithm of the starting precision
lorenz-horizon.excludes: errors from a wrong model, which the toy does not have

reflexive.definition: a published forecast that the forecast population reads and reacts to, so that publishing it changes the outcome it predicts
reflexive.excludes: a forecast kept private from the people it describes
